challenges.title: Module 1.1 — Foundational Querying (Store Footprint)
challenges.prompt:
The client wants to understand their footprint.
Write a query that returns the number of stores in the `stores` table.

Submit with:  train submit SELECT ...
challenges.hint: COUNT(*) counts rows. You have been doing this for eleven years.

challenges.title: Module 1.2 — Aggregation for Business Outcomes
challenges.prompt:
Return each store_id and its total transaction amount (SUM of `amount`)
from `transactions`. One row per store. Column order: store_id, total.
challenges.hint: GROUP BY store_id. The ordering of rows is not graded. Nothing about this is graded, really.
challenges.expected_sql: SELECT store_id, SUM(amount) FROM transactions GROUP BY store_id

challenges.title: Module 2.1 — snek Fundamentals: Log Parsing
challenges.prompt:
Write a snek function parse_line(line) that parses a PoS sync log line:

  '2026-11-02T09:14:03 STORE=0042 TERM=03 AMT=12.99'

and returns:

  {'store': '0042', 'term': '03', 'amt': 12.99}

`train submit` opens an editor. ^O writes it out, ^X submits.
challenges.hint: str.split() with no arguments splits on whitespace. Then split each piece on '='.

challenges.title: Module 2.2 — Filtering with Intent
challenges.prompt:
Return the `name` of every employee at store 42 who was hired
on or after 2020-01-01. Dates are ISO strings, so they compare as text.

(Tip from the course author: run `sql SELECT * FROM employees LIMIT 5`
to get a feel for the data first.)
challenges.expected_sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE store_id = 42 AND hired >= '2020-01-01'

challenges.title: Module 3.1 — Secure Coding: PCI-Adjacent Masking
challenges.prompt:
Write mask(value) that replaces every character except the last 4
with '*'. Values shorter than 5 characters are returned unchanged.

  mask('4111111111111111') -> '************1111'
  mask('abc')              -> 'abc'

Security is everyone's responsibility.

challenges.title: Module 3.2 — Data Quality Capstone
challenges.prompt:
Inventory can't be negative. Return the `sku` and `on_hand` of every
product with on_hand below zero.

Completing this module issues your Engineering Excellence certificate.
challenges.expected_sql: SELECT sku, on_hand FROM products WHERE on_hand < 0
